vesprite-vector-drawing-for-pixel-art-in.title: vesprite-vector-drawing-for-pixel-art-inside-aseprite
vesprite-vector-drawing-for-pixel-art-in.description_html:
VeSprite is a small vector editor inside Aseprite.

Pen tool

Click to place corners, drag to pull out a curve, click the first anchor to close.

Rect and Ellipse

Drag a box; hold Shift for a square or a circle. Snap decides where the corners may land.

Select and move

Drag an anchor to move it, drag the outline to move the whole shape. Ctrl+click adds, arrows nudge, box selects, Delete removes.

Anchor types

Corner, Smooth or Symmetric from one button (or C), handles you can pull, and a double click on the outline that inserts an anchor.

Layers

Layers with an eye, Add / Del / Dup / Up / Down, and the active one always in view.

Fill and stroke

Fill and stroke per layer, one-pixel outlines walked pixel-perfect, thicker ones expanded with caps and joins.

Gradients that become pixel art

Linear, radial, angular, diamond or reflected; pick the number of bands and the screen that breaks them: Bayer, blue noise, clustered, lines.

Blend modes and opacity

Nine blend modes and an opacity slider per layer, applied to the pixels below.

Auto close, zoom and pan

Auto close makes every Pen shape a filled one from the third anchor; the wheel zooms about the cursor, the middle button pans, Fit brings it all back.

Also

  • SVG in and out: paths, shapes, transforms and arcs in; one path per layer with colours, strokes, opacity, blend and gradients out.
  • Straight into the sprite: new layer, active cel or new sprite. Indexed and grayscale sprites get the nearest palette colours.
  • Its own .vesprite file; the drawing survives closing the window and closing Aseprite.

License

- Use VeSprite in any project: personal, commercial, client work, games  you sell.
- Everything you draw and export is yours. No attribution required.
- Install on every machine you own. One purchase per artist.
- Modify the source for your own use.

ghostframe-aseprite-extension.description_html:
Aseprite · inbetween assistant

GhostFrames

Not generative AI. GhostFrames does not create art from prompts. It runs optical-flow style frame interpolation (RIFE) between your keyframes.
Speed up your animation workflow with GhostFrames for Pose estimations. Generate intermediates on the timeline, then keep drawing where it matters, final frames or onion ghost guides.

License  CC0

GhostFrames is released under CC0 1.0 Universal. After purchase you may use, modify, redistribute, and include it in commercial projects with no attribution required.
The €9.97 price is for the packaged download on itch.io, not a restriction on usage rights. Third-party note: the bundled rife-ncnn-vulkan engine and RIFE model files keep their own licenses (MIT / upstream notices). Those components are not CC0. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md inside the package.
RIFE is a video frame-interpolation model estimates in-between frames from two images. It is not an image generator.

Faster inbetweens, your style stays yours

Select a frame range on the Aseprite timeline, run Interpolate frames…, and get intermediates in seconds. Use final frames when you want ready art ,effects, prototypes, or onion reference mode when you want a semi-transparent ghost guide to redraw over.

free-easy-interpolations-for-aseprite.title: free-easy-interpolations-for-aseprite
free-easy-interpolations-for-aseprite.description_html:
Easy Interpolation

Inbetween frames for Aseprite 



Easy Interpolation is a free Aseprite extension that generates inbetween frames for pixel art animation. Select two drawings on the timeline, right-click, and it creates the frames in between.

It works like a motion tween for Aseprite: the extension detects what changes between your two keyframes and interpolates it. You can tween cel position, opacity, pixel crossfade, rotation and scale around a clickable pivot. Every channel uses easing curves, ease in, ease out, quad, cubic, sine, expo, back, elastic, bounce, so the motion feels natural instead of linear.

Typical uses: smooth sprite movement for games, fade transitions, rotating coins or items, squash-and-stretch style scaling, breathing/idle animations, and quick inbetweens between two hand-drawn poses.

Crossfade needs an RGB sprite; position, opacity, rotation and scale also work in indexed and grayscale mode.




Free download. If it saves you time, check out my other Aseprite extensions. 



Easy Interpolation is free and MIT-licensed.
